title: Interstate banking deregulation on credit supply

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
The appropriate causal method to use here is a Difference-in-Differences (DID) approach. This method is well-suited for assessing policy impacts when a treatment is applied at a specific time to a defined group, and there is a comparable non-treated group. We compare the changes in outcomes for the treated group (deregulated states) relative to the control group (regulated states) before and after the intervention. The key assumption for the validity of DID is the "parallel trends assumption," which states that in the absence of the treatment, the difference between the treated and control groups would have remained constant over time.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(broom)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the CSV file
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s05_data.csv")

# Implement DID analysis using linear regression model
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated * post, data = data)

# Print summary of the model to get the coefficient of interest
coeftest(did_model, vcov = vcovHC(did_model, type = "HC1"))

# Conduct basic robustness check: Check for parallel trends
# Using pre-treatment periods to check for significant differences

# Subset for pre-treatment period (period < 4)
pre_treatment_data <- filter(data, period < 4)

# Run a placebo test (pre-trends test)
pre_trends_model <- lm(y ~ treated + factor(period), data = pre_treatment_data)

# Print summary to see if treated is significant, which it should not be
coeftest(pre_trends_model, vcov = vcovHC(pre_trends_model, type = "HC1"))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect a positive sign on the `treat_x_post` coefficient, indicating that deregulation is associated with an increase in the credit supply (measured as the loans-to-assets ratio) in the deregulated states. The magnitude will depend on how impactful the deregulation was in loosening credit restrictions; a moderate positive effect would be reasonable if prior restrictions were significant. However, this estimate should be interpreted while considering the overall economic and regulatory environment of the banking industry during the study period.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=deregulated states, control=still-regulated; shock=deregulation date
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Credit supply increases significantly after deregulation
